questions.prompt:
A 224 by 224 image with 16 by 16 patches yields 196 patch tokens before special tokens. Doubling each image dimension produces four times as many patches.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
A vision transformer splits an image into patches and embeds each patch with position information. Smaller patches retain finer detail but produce more tokens; preprocessing resolution changes both detail and cost.

Resolution must be budgeted in tokens as well as pixels.
keyPoints: Resolution must be budgeted in tokens as well as pixels.
A vision transformer splits an image into patches and embeds each patch with position information.

questions.prompt:
Two product images share the same background and near-identical captions. A model can learn the background shortcut instead of the distinguishing product feature.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Contrastive training brings paired image and text representations together while separating competing pairs. Success depends on pair quality and negatives; shared proximity reflects training associations rather than a guarantee of factual recognition.

Counterexamples can expose shortcuts in image-text alignment.
keyPoints: Counterexamples can expose shortcuts in image-text alignment.
Contrastive training brings paired image and text representations together while separating competing pairs.

questions.prompt:
A two-column policy is read across columns, combining an exception from one section with a rule from another.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
OCR produces text estimates, often with bounding boxes and confidence. Reading order, columns and headings must be reconstructed before chunking or a correct word stream can still yield an incorrect document meaning.

Document structure must survive text extraction.
keyPoints: Document structure must survive text extraction.
OCR produces text estimates, often with bounding boxes and confidence.

questions.prompt:
A revenue table labels its columns in thousands. An extracted value of 125 is incorrectly reported as 125 dollars instead of 125 thousand dollars.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Tables encode meaning through row headers, column headers, merged cells and units. Store that structure alongside values and retain the source location; isolated numeric chunks lose the relationships needed to answer questions.

Numeric retrieval needs headers and units.
keyPoints: Numeric retrieval needs headers and units.
Tables encode meaning through row headers, column headers, merged cells and units.

questions.prompt:
An 8 kHz phone recording is resampled to 48 kHz. The file has more samples but does not gain the high-frequency detail of a studio recording.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Sampling rate determines how often a waveform is measured; a spectrogram describes frequency content across time windows. Resampling requires filtering to avoid aliasing and cannot restore frequencies absent from the original recording.

Upsampling does not recover lost audio detail.
keyPoints: Upsampling does not recover lost audio detail.
Sampling rate determines how often a waveform is measured; a spectrogram describes frequency content across time windows.

questions.prompt:
A transcript gets most filler words right but changes a medication quantity. Its overall WER looks acceptable despite an important semantic mistake.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Word error rate counts substitutions, deletions and insertions divided by reference word count. Normalize references consistently, and inspect meaningful entities separately because aggregate WER can hide dangerous number or name errors.

Aggregate transcription accuracy should be supplemented with critical-entity checks.
keyPoints: Aggregate transcription accuracy should be supplemented with critical-entity checks.
Word error rate counts substitutions, deletions and insertions divided by reference word count.

questions.prompt:
A one-second warning appears in a video sampled every ten seconds and is never observed.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Sparse sampling lowers compute but can miss brief events. Choose sampling based on event duration, supplement it with change detection, and evaluate missed-event rates rather than only sampled-frame accuracy.

Sampling policy determines which events can be observed.
keyPoints: Sampling policy determines which events can be observed.
Sparse sampling lowers compute but can miss brief events.

questions.prompt:
A subtitle track is shifted by three seconds, causing an instruction to be linked to the following action.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Video reasoning requires ordered timestamps and alignment between audio, frames and subtitles. Constant clock offsets and drift can associate speech with the wrong event; retain the original timebase when transforming media.

Cross-modal timestamps must be validated before reasoning about events.
keyPoints: Cross-modal timestamps must be validated before reasoning about events.
Video reasoning requires ordered timestamps and alignment between audio, frames and subtitles.

questions.prompt:
A product photo search benefits from visual similarity, while a serial-number query needs exact text matching.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
A joint embedding space supports cross-modal retrieval, while separate indexes can preserve specialized signals such as exact OCR strings. Choose indexes by query needs and measure each modality's contribution.

Different query types may require different retrieval signals.
keyPoints: Different query types may require different retrieval signals.
A joint embedding space supports cross-modal retrieval, while separate indexes can preserve specialized signals such as exact OCR strings.

questions.prompt:
OCR search produces scores near 20 and image search scores near 0.8. Adding them directly makes text dominate regardless of relevance.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Late fusion combines candidate rankings from multiple retrievers. Raw scores may have incompatible scales; rank-based fusion avoids assuming they are calibrated probabilities. Tune fusion on labeled relevance judgments.

Raw scores from different retrievers are not automatically comparable.
keyPoints: Raw scores from different retrievers are not automatically comparable.
Late fusion combines candidate rankings from multiple retrievers.

questions.prompt:
An image encoder changes resolution but its cache key includes only the file hash, so old features remain in use.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Version image resizing, audio resampling and OCR settings together with model inputs. Cache keys must include transformations and model versions, or incompatible features can be silently reused.

Cache identity must include preprocessing and encoder versions.
keyPoints: Cache identity must include preprocessing and encoder versions.
Version image resizing, audio resampling and OCR settings together with model inputs.

questions.prompt:
A team deletes meeting audio but keeps unrestricted transcripts containing the same confidential discussion.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Images and recordings may include faces, voices, location metadata and incidental personal information. Minimize collection, restrict access and define retention for originals and derived artifacts, including embeddings and transcripts.

Derived artifacts need privacy controls as well as original media.
keyPoints: Derived artifacts need privacy controls as well as original media.
Images and recordings may include faces, voices, location metadata and incidental personal information.
